Blood sugar: Nutrients from the last meal enter the bloodstream and blood sugar rises.\nInsulin: Insulin works actively to move rising blood sugar into the cells.\nEnergy: The body uses energy directly from recently eaten food.

Blood sugar drop: Available sugar in the blood begins to decrease.\nLiver support: The liver releases stored glycogen to help keep blood sugar balanced.\nFeelings: Mild hunger and small energy fluctuations may begin.
Glycogen use: Sugar stores in the liver are mostly reduced.\nMetabolism: The body starts preparing to use fat as a main energy source.\nSymptoms: Mild headache, distraction, or bad breath may occur.

Ketosis begins: The body starts using fat for energy.\nAutophagy: Cells begin cleaning damaged parts and renewing themselves.\nGrowth hormone: Levels may rise to support lean muscle preservation and tissue repair.

This policy summarizes what information Fitto processes and why it is used.
Account information, profile details, health goals, daily records, social posts, comments, and messaging data may be stored to provide app features.
Your information is used for personalized goals, profile experience, social interactions, reminders, and app security.
Posts, comments, likes, and profile information you share may be visible to other users depending on your visibility settings.
Messaging data is stored to provide the chat experience. Users you block are limited from reaching you and interacting with you.
When you delete your account, identity and health information is cleaned. Some old social content may remain anonymously as Deleted User to preserve social consistency.

Fitto uses Firebase services for authentication, database, file storage, and online presence features. Fitto AI may send target and onboarding information to an AI service to generate personalized answers.
Data is protected with Firebase security rules, user sessions, and reauthentication checks for sensitive actions.
By using Fitto, you agree to these terms.
You are responsible for the accuracy of your account information and the security of your account.
Calories, goals, and nutrition suggestions in Fitto are for informational purposes only. They are not medical advice.
Insults, harassment, spam, misleading content, others’ images, or unauthorized personal information are not allowed.
You are responsible for the posts, comments, images, and other content you share.
You can block users who bother you. Some interactions may be restricted to keep the community safe.
Account deletion cannot be undone. Personal information is cleaned after deletion; some social records may remain anonymized.
Fitto features may be improved, changed, or removed over time.

It is suitable for people who want a more structured routine, more regular meal timing, and a sustainable eating model. It is also one of the most preferred methods for beginners.

First, try increasing your water intake. Unsweetened herbal tea or black coffee may also help. Mild hunger is normal in the first days; however, if you feel dizzy or overly weak, do not force the plan.

Yes. During the fasting period, unsweetened black coffee and allowed drinks like mineral water can support you. You should avoid calorie-containing additions because they can break the fasting structure.
The 15:9 method includes fasting for 15 hours and eating within a 9-hour window. It is a slightly more disciplined but still flexible transition after 12:12.
Supports a gentle move to longer fasting.
Fits easily into a daily routine.
Suitable for users who are comfortable with 12:12 and want to move toward a slightly longer fasting period.

Yes, especially for users who are already comfortable with 12:12. Narrowing the eating window gradually can make the transition easier.
Will 15 hours of fasting be difficult?
It may feel challenging at first. Drinking water, sleeping well, and getting enough protein and fiber during the eating window can help.
How many meals should I eat on 15:9?
Usually 2 main meals and 1 snack can work well, but meal count can be adjusted according to personal goals and routine.
The 6:1 method focuses on eating in a balanced way for 6 days and following a more controlled calorie pattern for 1 day. It is based on weekly balance rather than daily fasting hours.
Does not restrict every day heavily.
Supports consistency with one controlled day.
Suitable for users who do not want daily time-based fasting and prefer a weekly balance approach.
When you follow this plan, 1 controlled day and 6 balanced eating days are tracked weekly.
What should a controlled day look like?
A controlled day should be lighter and planned. Instead of extreme restriction, focusing on vegetables, protein, and water is more sustainable.
Yes. 6:1 focuses on a weekly pattern rather than tracking fasting hours every day.
Can I change the controlled day?
Yes, you can adjust the controlled day according to your weekly schedule. This can later be personalized inside the app.

Is the custom %1$d:%2$d plan right for me?
It can work if it fits your daily routine and energy level. If you are new to fasting, starting with a shorter fasting duration and increasing gradually may feel more comfortable.
Can I change this plan later?
Yes. The purpose of a custom plan is flexibility. If it feels difficult, you can reduce the fasting duration; if it feels comfortable, you can increase it gradually.
Why does the start time default to 20:00?
20:00 is a natural closing point after dinner for many users. Later, we can also make this start time selectable by the user.

The DASH diet is a balanced eating approach that supports blood pressure management. It focuses on vegetables, fruits, whole grains, low-fat dairy, legumes, fish, and nuts while aiming to reduce sodium intake.
Focuses on balanced food choices that support blood pressure management.
Encourages reducing salt and highly processed foods.
Includes vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and protein sources in a balanced way.
Aim to keep daily sodium intake generally under 2,300 mg.
Choose fresh and lower-sodium foods instead of highly processed packaged foods.
If you have blood pressure, kidney, or heart concerns, get support from a doctor or dietitian.
The 12:12 method involves fasting for 12 hours and eating within a 12-hour window. It is an ideal, balanced, and sustainable fasting routine for beginners.
Convenient and practical for those new to fasting.
Provides more balanced energy levels throughout the day.
Can be easily maintained over the long term.
Suitable for beginners, those looking to build a healthy routine, and anyone who wants to feel better with a light fasting schedule.
By following this plan, you can maintain a balanced weekly 12:12 routine.
Will the 12:12 plan help me lose weight?
Yes, when combined with a balanced diet and calorie control, the 12:12 plan can support weight management.
What should I do if I feel dizzy while fasting?
First, increase your water intake. If symptoms persist, the best approach is to stop the plan and consult a healthcare professional.
Can I fast if I am taking medication?
If you use medication regularly, you must consult your doctor before starting intermittent fasting.

The MIND diet combines the strengths of the Mediterranean and DASH diets with a focus on brain health. It prioritizes leafy greens, berries such as blueberries, nuts, legumes, whole grains, fish, and olive oil.
Focuses on brain-friendly foods as part of a balanced routine.
Highlights leafy greens and berry-group fruits.

Plant-based nutrition centers meals around vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains, nuts, and seeds. The goal is to plan protein, fiber, healthy fats, and micronutrients from plant-forward sources in a balanced way.
Supports higher fiber intake through vegetables, legumes, and whole grains.
Highlights plant fats and fiber while reducing reliance on saturated fat sources.
Offers a more environmentally friendly and long-term eating pattern.
Do not ignore vitamin B12 sources; reliable supplements or fortified foods are important for vegan patterns.
Rotate legumes, tofu, tempeh, quinoa, nuts, and seeds for protein variety.
Track iron, calcium, omega-3, and vitamin D sources intentionally.

Keeps carbohydrates, protein, and healthy fats in balance.

The elimination diet is an approach that helps identify potential triggers by temporarily removing specific foods that may cause discomfort, tracking symptoms, and then reintroducing foods one by one. This plan should specifically be followed with professional guidance.
Helps track more systematically which foods may be linked to discomfort.
Makes it easier to monitor symptoms such as bloating, gas, or sensitivity.
Provides a clearer tracking process by reintroducing foods individually.
Create a flexible routine that fits your daily rhythm. You can start with a balanced plan and adjust it over time.

The ketogenic diet aims to put the body into a state of ketosis by reducing carbohydrate intake. In this routine, fats are used as the primary energy source, which can support weight management.
Promotes the body’s use of fats for energy.
The fat and protein-focused structure can help you stay full for longer.
Can help maintain more stable blood sugar levels.
You should consider your health status before starting a ketogenic diet.
Reducing carbohydrates too quickly can cause headaches and fatigue.
Consulting a doctor or dietitian is recommended for long-term use.
Seek professional support before removing foods entirely for an unnecessarily long time.
Try foods one by one during the reintroduction phase and note any symptoms.
Consult a doctor or dietitian if you have severe reactions, suspected allergies, or chronic conditions.
